newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's NSW seen in for bumper harvest.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's NSW seen in for bumper harvest.

text.p: Leading Australian grain handler and trader GrainCorp predicted a seven to eight million tonne 1996/97 grain harvest for the state of New South Wales (NSW).
This would make it the state's second largest grain harvest on record.
The state's north and south were both estimated to produce 3.5 to 4.0 million tonnes of grain in the coming harvest, GrainCorp general manager Tom Keene said in a statement.
GrainCorp was preparing for an increase in receivals of more than 35 percent on the last harvest, to between 6.0 and 6.5 million tonnes of grain, he said.
This would compare with the previous record of 8.3 million tonnes in receivals in 1983/84.
GrainCorp had brought forward an extra A$1.34 million worth of improvements in addition to the A$10 million announced earlier this year to help streamline receivals at additional NSW sites, he said.
With last year's larger than average harvest, there were concerns that sites would not be cleared for the coming harvest, he said.
Earlier predictions were for up to 1.5 million tonnes of grain carried over in the system, he said.
"To ensure the system is largely free of last season's grain, GrainCorp is working closely with the Australian Wheat Board, the NSW Grains Board and other customers to clear sites," he said.

"This programme is working well and to date more than 2.8 million tonnes of grain have been moved out of the system." GrainCorp now estimates stock levels in the system before harvest will be at minimum levels with only 250,000 to 500,000 tonnes of strategic carryover.

Currently between five and seven 2,000 tonne trains a day were working to move grain from outlying sites to port, while GrainCorp was hiring about 900 casual harvest workers as grain handlers, weighbridge clerks and silo managers.
"There is a real sense of optimism in rural NSW over the developing wheat, barley and other crops," Keene said.
Wheat and barley are Australia's major grain crops. They grow over winter and are harvested in summer, peaking around December-January.
